skill.name: dispatching-parallel-agents
skill.description: Guides users to split independent debugging or implementation work across parallel AI agents.
skill.summary: Coordinate independent AI agent tasks and merge their results with conflict checks.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

content.value_statement: Independent failures waste time when one agent investigates them sequentially. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code split work safely and merge results.
actual_capabilities: Explains when parallel agent work is appropriate for independent failures.
Shows how to group test failures by subsystem or problem domain.
Provides a structure for focused agent prompts with scope and expected output.
Defines an integration workflow for summaries, conflict checks, and test runs.
Lists cases where sequential investigation is safer than parallel dispatch.
limitations: Does not provide executable automation for launching agents.
Requires the user to judge whether failures are independent.
Does not prevent agents from making conflicting edits.
Works best when each task has clear files, failures, and constraints.

use_cases.title: Triage Independent Test Failures
use_cases.description: Split unrelated failing test files across focused agents, then review and merge each result.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Refactor Follow-Up
use_cases.description: Assign separate post-refactor issues to agents when each subsystem can be fixed independently.

use_cases.title: Teach Agent Delegation
use_cases.description: Use the pattern to show teams how to write scoped prompts for concurrent AI work.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Parallel Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these failures and group them by independent problem domain. Tell me which ones can be assigned to separate agents and why.

prompt_templates.title: Create Agent Assignments
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn grouped failures into scoped tasks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create one focused agent assignment per independent domain. Include scope, goal, constraints, expected output, and files to avoid.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Agent Results
prompt_templates.scenario: Review multiple returned summaries before merging changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these agent summaries. Identify conflicts, missing verification, risky edits, and the order for integrating the fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Parallel Debugging Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a large failure set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a parallel debugging plan for these failures. Separate related and independent work, assign agents, define merge checks, and list final verification.

output_examples.input: Three unrelated test files fail after a refactor.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend one agent per test file, with each prompt limited to that file and its direct subsystem.

output_examples.input: Two failures may share the same root cause.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend investigating them together first, because parallel fixes could duplicate work or conflict.

output_examples.input: Agents return three summaries after concurrent debugging.
output_examples.output: The skill would guide the user to read each summary, check file overlap, run the full suite, and spot check assumptions.

best_practices: Dispatch agents only after confirming the work does not share state.
Give each agent a narrow scope, clear goal, constraints, and expected summary.
Review summaries and run the full test suite before accepting combined changes.
anti_patterns: Do not split work when one fix could resolve several failures.
Do not send agents vague requests such as fixing all tests.
Do not merge parallel results without checking conflicts and verification gaps.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when two or more tasks are independent and can be investigated without shared state or sequencing.

faq.question: Does it launch agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow and prompt structure for tools that already support agent delegation.

faq.question: Can it help with failing tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It is especially useful when different test files fail for unrelated reasons.

faq.question: What makes a good agent task?
faq.answer: A good task has one problem domain, enough context, strict constraints, and a clear requested summary.

faq.question: What is the main risk?
faq.answer: The main risk is conflicting edits when tasks are not truly independent or when constraints are too broad.

faq.question: How should I finish after agents return?
faq.answer: Read every summary, check for overlapping edits, run the full suite, and spot check the final behavior.
